items.prompt:
A fossil is:
A) A living animal
B) The preserved remains or trace of a once-living organism
C) A kind of rock with no life
D) A type of cell
items.answer: B) The preserved remains or trace of a once-living organism

steps: Fossils are preserved remains or traces of past life.

items.prompt:
Fossils are most often found in:
A) Sedimentary rock
B) Clouds
C) Ocean water
D) The air

steps: Layers of sedimentary rock preserve fossils.

items.prompt:
In undisturbed rock layers, the oldest fossils are:
A) At the top
B) In the deepest layers
C) Floating
D) Not there

steps: Deeper layers formed first and hold older fossils.

items.prompt:
A species that dies out completely is said to be:
A) Extinct
B) Reproducing
C) A producer
D) A fossil fuel

A type of organism appears in older layers but is absent from all younger layers. This shows:
A) Its extinction
B) Its increase
C) A mutation
D) Nothing

steps: Disappearing from later layers indicates extinction.

items.prompt:
Simpler fossils appear in deeper layers and more complex ones in higher layers. This suggests:
A) Organisms never change
B) Organisms changed over time
C) Rocks are alive
D) Fossils move up

steps: Changing forms from older to younger layers show change over time.

items.prompt:
Why does a deeper fossil generally indicate an older organism in undisturbed rock?
A) Deeper rock is warmer
B) Deeper layers were deposited first, so they are older
C) Deeper fossils are larger
D) Depth has no meaning
items.answer: B) Deeper layers were deposited first, so they are older

steps: Sediment builds up over time, so deeper layers and their fossils are older.

items.prompt:
Which list best describes patterns found in the fossil record?
A) Only the weather
B) Existence, diversity, extinction, and change of life forms over time
C) Only the colors of rocks
D) The future of life
items.answer: B) Existence, diversity, extinction, and change of life forms over time

steps: The fossil record shows these patterns across Earth's history.
